historical.ss_analysis: Steffel <ss> is analyzed by Merrill as intervocalic voiceless [s], not a geminate.

independent_e_i_variation.statement: Steffel's documented vowel alternations include e~i; Merrill notes that e/i differences are also relevant to modern Rarámuri variety distinctions.
independent_e_i_variation.scope: historical internal variation; not a directional sound law

src02.provenance_warning: SRC-02 file identity unresolved and probably within a Hilton/pre-2016 lexicographic lineage.

community.source: SEP 2010 Awilichi bawi / El origen del agua
community.independence: independent community usage outside the unresolved SRC-02/Hilton lineage

phonology.process: optional /e/ raising to [i] in pretonic and posttonic position
phonology.relevance: the initial vowel of nesé/nisé is pretonic

integrated_formal_assessment.consonants: no unresolved ss~s quantity mismatch after Merrill normalization

why_grade_A: The apparent historical <ss> complication disappears under a published phonetic analysis.
Historical Steffel data independently contain e~i vowel alternation outside the target word.
A modern independent grammar documents the more specific pretonic /e/->[i] alternation in Rarámuri.
Historical and modern forms align in final stress and caretaker/shepherd semantics.
Independent Balleza community usage confirms nise’ami in the shepherd domain outside the SRC-02/Hilton lineage.
remaining_limits: Grade A is an evidential-architecture judgment, not a declaration of cognacy.
No single diachronic law e>i is claimed; historical e~i and modern pretonic raising only make the correspondence independently plausible.
A geographically and chronologically ordered correspondence set is still desirable before a publication-level cognacy statement.
The SEP community text is lexical-semantic evidence, not an explicit morphological analysis.
next_tests: Collect additional historical-modern e~i pairs with stress and geography documented.
Search intermediate and regional sources for nese/nise variants and caretaker/shepherd derivatives.
Model whether the modern i is phonological surface raising, lexicalized dialectal vowel, or inherited variant.
